# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

## Problem

`wl doctor prune --days N` hard-deletes items locally, but the next `wl sync` re-adds them all from the remote ref, because `mergeWorkItems` (src/sync.ts) re-imports every remote item missing locally (`if (!localItem) { mergedMap.set(remoteItem.id, remoteItem); }`). There is no `--no-pull` and prune has no push/rewrite path.

## Observed (2026-08-13)

- Ran `wl doctor prune --days 0` → 1,034 items hard-deleted locally (2941 → 1907 items)
- Ran `wl sync` → 'Work items added: 1034' — all resurrected from `refs/worklog/data` (back to 2941)
- Net result: prune is a no-op in a synced setup; items remain soft-deleted forever (the 'deleted but not pruned' backlog)

## Proposed fix

Add `--push` (or auto-push) to `wl doctor prune` that, after hard-deleting locally, rewrites the remote worklog ref with the pruned local state — mirroring `doctor foreign-items --apply --push` which already uses `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (src/sync.ts:1130).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl doctor prune --days N --push` leaves the remote ref without the pruned items
- [ ] A subsequent `wl sync` does NOT resurrect the pruned items
- [ ] `--dry-run` unchanged; default remains no-push (safe)
- [ ] Unit/integration test covers prune+push against a temp git repo
data.title: wl doctor prune cannot persist: sync re-adds pruned items from remote ref

# Implement auto-downgrade of critical priority on terminal transitions

## Goal
When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state (status=completed or stage=in_review), automatically downgrade its priority to `high`.

## Implementation Details

### 1. Downgrade Logic

Add a helper function to detect and perform the auto-downgrade:
- Location: `packages/shared/src/database.ts` alongside the existing `cascadePriorityDowngrade`
- Function: `downgradeIfTerminal(item)` or inline check
- Logic: if item's new state has `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` AND `priority=critical`, set `priority=high`

### 2. Call Sites

Invoke from terminal-transition paths:
- `src/commands/update.ts` — after status/stage update, before response
- `src/commands/close.ts` — after close logic, before response

Prefer explicit call sites to avoid interfering with internal DB `update()` cascade calls.

### 3. Reporting

Report the downgrade in both output formats, mirroring the existing `downgradedChildren` pattern:
- JSON output: add `downgradedItem` field (or similar) with `{id, priority}` 
- Human-readable: add a summary line like `Downgraded priority from critical to high`

### 4. Constraints

- Only affect `critical` → `high` downgrade
- No change to other priorities (high/medium/low remain untouched)
- Only trigger on terminal transitions: `--status completed`, `--stage in_review`, or `wl close`
- Non-terminal transitions (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must NOT change priority

### Key Files
- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — helper function location
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — priority constants

data.description:
As an operator, I do not want a transient failure in the downtime dispatch pipeline to strand a work item in `in_progress` with no agent working it and no automatic recovery.

## Background

- dispatchClaimedTier (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts) pipeline: CAS claim → marker write → spawn.
- Gap 1 from the dispatch decision-point evaluation: if the marker write fails (D16) AFTER the CAS claim succeeds, the outcome is reason 'marker-write-failed' and the item stays `in_progress` — but the claim is never rolled back. The item is then invisible to every later tier: plan/implement tiers select `status === 'open'`, the audit tier selects `completed`. Only manual intervention recovers it.
- Same class of issue on 'spawn-failed' (D17): the marker stands (kind `implement`/`plan`/`audit` at the dispatched-at stage), so even after a human reverts the item to `open`, the dispatched-marker exclusion keeps it out of selection until the stage changes — a transient send-to-pi.sh failure (e.g. ENOENT) permanently removes a never-worked item from the idle-slot queue.
- Existing design intent (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT design point 2): "an unmarked item is never dispatched" — this is sound; the gap is the missing RECOVERY path, not the fail-closed abort.

## Design notes

- Option A (rollback): on 'marker-write-failed', restore the item to its pre-claim state (CAS reverse: `wl update <id> --status open --if-status in_progress [--if-stage ...]`) so the next idle period can select it again.
- Option B (requeue for spawn-failed): on 'spawn-failed', write a distinct marker variant (e.g. `outcome: 'spawn-failed'` entries are already appended) and have the marker-exclusion readers treat a spawn-failed marker as NON-excluding (item is re-eligible) while still logging the failure — the rolling log already distinguishes attempted vs opened (WL-0MSLWJ3I70031Z8U AC2).
- Both options preserve the fail-closed invariant (a marker-less item is never dispatched twice concurrently); the CAS claim already serializes re-selection.
- Decide and document whether the re-dispatch window should be immediate (next idle) or after a short backoff to avoid spawn-failure hot loops.

## Acceptance criteria

1. 'marker-write-failed' leaves the item in a state selectable by a future tier (rolled back to open+original stage, or equivalently recovered) — never stranded in_progress with no agent.
2. 'spawn-failed' does not permanently exclude the item from selection; the failure trace remains in the rolling log and the outcome is still not success.
3. No regression: an item with a STANDING success marker is still excluded (never double-dispatched); CAS claim still serializes concurrent panes.
4. Tests cover marker-write-failed and spawn-failed recovery paths end-to-end (claim → failure → re-selection on the next idle period).
data.title: Downtime dispatch: recover items stranded by marker-write-failed or spawn-failed (no permanent->in_progress stranding)

## Goal

Implement the herdr hydrator module (packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts): every 30s (and on worklist focus-resume) it fetches all in_progress work items, matches each against work-item IDs in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace, and demotes any item with no matching pane per the signal-based rule (AC3 of parent WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI). Pure decision functions + orchestration with injectable deps; fail-open at every boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes) returns WL-[0-9A-Z]+ IDs found in pane labels.
2. isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes) returns true iff the ID appears in a running pane's label in any tab of the current workspace; workspace filtering via herdr pane list --workspace <id> / HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID env var.
3. decideDemotion(workItem, blockers): stage in_review → {status: completed, stage: in_review}; active outbound blocker (target not completed/deleted, stage not in_review/done, per isDependencyActive in packages/shared/src/database.ts) → {status: blocked, stage: plan_complete (or best compatible)}; else → {status: open, stage: intake_complete}; stage always chosen per src/config.ts compatibility.
4. runHydrationOnce(deps): fetches wl list --status in_progress, fetches panes, computes demotions, applies each via wl update (status+stage); an item with a matching pane is never touched.
5. Fail-open: wl/pane CLI missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output → skip the entire cycle with a log; the function never throws; no demotion happens on untrustworthy evidence.
6. All hydrator.test.ts tests pass; full project suite passes.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts — new module
- packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts — reuse runWl/extractJson/extractItems
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts — orchestration precedent
- src/commands/dep.ts + packages/shared/src/database.ts — dependency semantics (reference only)
- src/config.ts — status/stage compatibility (reference only)

## Minimal Implementation

1. Pure helpers: extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles, isActivePaneMatch, decideDemotion (status, stage) pair.
2. runHydrationOnce(deps) with injectable {runWl, runPaneList, now, log}; fetch in_progress; fetch panes filtered to workspace; outbound-edge stage fetch per blocker candidate (wl dep list carries status only — fetch stage via wl show for each edge not completed/deleted).
3. Apply demotions; wrap whole cycle in try/catch that logs and returns without demoting.

## Dependencies

- Requires F1 (hydrator.test.ts — written first; suite must pass to close)
- Requires F0 (pane-title format amendment — ID must survive truncation)

# Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork`) and the Herdr extension selection list (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` → `worklist.ts`) disagree on "most important item" because the dispatcher maintains its own tier ordering (`wl next --stage …` per tier + `wl list` audit query) instead of reusing the Herdr list. The project needs the dispatcher to consume the Herdr list head so the two selectors agree by construction. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`" scope per producer determination WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 (2026-09-02).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — needs a single trustworthy queue; the item dispatched during downtime was visible at the top of `prefix+l` and reflects declared prioritization intent.
- **Herdr user browsing `prefix+l`** — expects downtime work to track exactly what the visible list shows, so automated work does not appear arbitrary.
- **Maintainer of herdr / downtime-worker / wl next** — needs a single ranking contract; ranking logic lives only in the fetcher/smart-selection/grouping/database pipeline.

Example user stories:
- As a producer, I want the downtime dispatcher to pick the first item shown in the Herdr list, so automated work follows the priority I already see.
- As a herdr user, when downtime dispatches `/skill:implement WL-XYZ`, I want WL-XYZ to have been at the head of the Herdr list, so I understand why it was chosen.
- As a maintainer, I want the ranking contract documented as "dispatcher == Herdr list head" so future safety gates are evaluated as filters, not a competing ranking.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dispatcher consumes Herdr list head** — `dispatchDowntimeWork` (and any coordination-leader path) derives its candidate from the Herdr selection list head rather than a separate tier ordering / stage-scoped `wl next` / `wl list` audit query. No second ranking implementation remains on the dispatch path.
2. **No duplicate ranking; gates are filters** — tier ordering / `wl next --stage` per-tier calls / audit `wl list` ranking are no longer used to pick "most important". Any safety gates that must remain (code-freeze skip, dispatched-marker exclusion, active-audit single-flight, per-process single-flight / CAS claim) act as sequential filters on the Herdr-ordered candidates. If no Herdr-ordered candidate passes the filters, the dispatcher reports "no candidate" rather than falling back to a separate ranking.
3. **Herdr list remains sole ranking path** — `fetchNextItems` / `selectWorkItems` / `regroupWorkItems` stay the sole ranking path (mandatory-always for critical + `completed`/`in_review`, `browseItemCount` windowing of "other" items, grouping logic, `reSort`/`computeScore` as used by the fetcher). No `wl next`/`database.ts` scoring change is required to fix the divergence; if `fetchNextItems` delegates to `wl next` internally that internal detail is acceptable — the observable contract is "dispatcher == Herdr list head".
4. **Contract documented** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` (and `src/commands/next.ts` help if it references dispatcher selection) state explicitly: dispatcher selects the first dispatchable item from the Herdr selection list; any remaining safety override (e.g. code-freeze) is documented as a skip/filter on that sequence, not a ranking.
5. **No regression; observable agreement proven** — existing `wl next` / herdr fetcher/grouping / downtime-worker fixtures pass; a reproducible sampling script shows `wl next -n` / Herdr list / downtime pick agree (downtime picks the list head after filtering) on a fixture. Dispatched-marker / code-freeze / single-flight gating still respected as filters on the Herdr sequence.

## Constraints

- Zero npm deps for herdr; `smart-selection.ts`/`grouping.ts` duplicated per TUI stays in sync with `src/commands/*` if touched.
- `browseItemCount` clamping (1–50) and root-only / `done`-exclusion rules respected.
- Do not fork a second ranking; reuse the Herdr list pipeline.
- Investigation only touched the prior item (WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q); this item carries the implementation.
- Backwards compat: existing dispatched-marker / code-freeze gating semantics preserved as filters.

## Existing state

- **Herdr list:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` runs `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` (auto `reSort` unless `--no-re-sort`), merges mandatory subsets via `fetchMandatorySubsets` (`wl list --priority critical --root-only` and `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`), applies `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` (root-only, `stage != done`, mandatory always shown, `browseItemCount` limits only "other" items), and regroups with `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` / `assignItemGroups` (Critical Group N / Group N / Idea / Other / In Review). Rendered via `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- **Downtime dispatcher:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork` — tier order audit → implement (`wl next --stage plan_complete` with risk/effort caps) → plan (`wl next --stage intake_complete`) → fallback idea (`wl next --stage idea`); audit tier uses `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` with 7-day recency / dispatched-marker / active-audit / code-freeze gates; pre-dispatch CAS claim, per-process single-flight, scheduled-prompts tier, round-robin cursor, cooldowns.
- **Shared scoring:** `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (`computeScore`/`reSort`/`filterCandidates`/`findNextWorkItemFromItems`) and `src/commands/next.ts` auto `reSort` — shared by `wl next` but not required to change for this contract; the observable contract is Herdr list head.
- All divergence gaps mapped in WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q (cap 32 / mandatory merge / stage-scoped calls / audit `wl list` source / tier order / risk-effort gates / code-freeze tri-state, etc.) — eliminated by consuming the Herdr order directly.

## Desired change

Replace the dispatcher's independent tier ordering with consumption of the Herdr selection list head:

- Refactor `downtime-worker.ts` to invoke (or share code with) the Herdr fetcher/selection pipeline to obtain the ordered candidate sequence, then apply only the necessary safety filters (code-freeze, dispatched-marker, single-flight/active-audit) sequentially on that sequence.
- Remove or dead-code the tier-ordering / per-stage `wl next` / audit `wl list` ranking path from the dispatch decision (or leave only as unused fallback behind a feature flag with a clear deprecation note).
- Document the contract ("dispatcher == Herdr list head; filters, not ranking") in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — Herdr selection pipeline reused by dispatcher
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — mandatory-always + browseItemCount logic
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — regroupWorkItems / assignItemGroups ordering
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — rendering consuming grouped selection
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatchDowntimeWork to be refactored to consume list head (+ fixtures)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — computeScore/reSort/filterCandidates as used by fetcher (not dispatcher ranking)
- `src/commands/next.ts` / `src/commands/grouping.ts` — wl next entry point as used by fetcher
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher contract doc
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr list contract doc

## Related work

- Investigation: WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q — downtime dispatcher vs herdr selection list divergence (producer determination revised 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, superseding WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS) → follow-up direction is this item.
- WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX — counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect (symptom of cap/mandatory interaction; not blocking but shares fetcher context)
- WL-0MS8XL3EW006Y04G / WL-0MSKCRX730052iiw / WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G / WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR — Herdr smart selection / in_review / root-only rules shaping mandatory set
- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 / WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG — implement tier + risk/effort filters wired into wl next / dispatcher (removed or converted to filters in this work)
- WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY / WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN / WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — dispatched-marker exclusion, conditional claim, dispatch logging (preserved as filters)
- WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6 — priority-first with round-robin tie-break (cursor handling to reconcile with Herdr order)
- RCA docs: `downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`, `downtime-disable-incident-rca-2026-08-22.md` — prior tier/re-dispatch incidents

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "selection list" means herdr `prefix+l` Work Items list (`fetchNextItems` path); "downtime dispatcher" means `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier loop in `downtime-worker.ts` (including coordination leader path if any).
- Assumption: producer wants a single notion of "most important" — confirmed 2026-09-02 (Herdr list canonical; dispatcher consumes head).
- Risk: code-freeze / audit safety behavior at head — if the list head must be skipped, the skip order must be explicit and remain a filter on the Herdr sequence; document clearly.
- Risk: `in_review` mandatory-always items in the list — dispatcher taking the head must still respect `completed`/`in_review` dispatchability; filter vs ranking distinction must be explicit to avoid re-dispatching audits.
- Risk: spare-capacity / idle-budget / round-robin cursor logic must be reconciled as filters or removed; otherwise a second ordering re-emerges.
- Scope-creep risk: unifying ranking touches herdr selection and downtime-worker — keep scope to dispatcher-consumes-head; do not rework scoring or grouping unless required for the contract. Extra opportunities → new work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When you say 'most important,' do you mean the Herdr list order or the dispatcher tier order?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, rescoping WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2; supersedes WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS): **Herdr extension selection list order is authoritative** (`fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems`). Dispatcher selects the first item in that list — no second ranking. Source: producer comment WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 on WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q.
- Q2: "Should the two selectors be unified to one shared ranking, or should the dispatcher intentionally differ (e.g. audit-first)?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): **Unified on the Herdr list** — single source of truth; dispatcher consumes the list head. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`". Source: same producer determination.
- Q3: "For sampling, which `browseItemCount` / `wl next -n` window and which worklog root should be the reference?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS as affirmed by WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): **LGTM** — default `browseItemCount` / ContextHub root / `wl next -n 20` accepted as sampling reference. Source: producer comment on WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q.

No open questions. Interview skipped — seed context and revised producer determination (WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1) already provide a clear, testable brief.
data.title: Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head (supersedes wl next unification)

# Child 1: Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn

Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 (mechanism 1).

## Problem statement

`batchUpdateSortIndices` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769`) runs `UPDATE workitems SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ?` with a single shared `now` for every item whose sortIndex changed. Re-sort runs automatically on `wl next` (unless `--no-re-sort`), on create/update, so routine queue reads rewrite `updatedAt` on dozens of items at once (observed: 13 items at `2026-09-11T07:34:26.956Z`, 88 items at `2026-09-11T08:33:19.554Z`).

The audit-freshness rule (`database.ts:644`, WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5: audit counts only if `auditedAt >= updatedAt`) then treats those items as edited-after-audit. Concrete victim: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V audited "Ready to close: Yes" 2026-09-03 now carries `updatedAt` 2026-09-11, so its passing audit reads stale and the item lingers in the open queue. Recency-weighted scoring (`database.ts:2215-2216`) is also polluted.

## Users

- **Producer/operator:** a "Ready to close: Yes" item must stay ready across mechanical re-sorts.
- **Heartbeat/audit pipeline:** must not re-audit items whose only change is sortIndex.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `batchUpdateSortIndices` (and the `database.ts:755-767` single-item re-sort path) no longer bump `updatedAt` when the only change is `sortIndex`. Semantic edits elsewhere still bump `updatedAt` as today.
- [ ] Regression test: audit an item "Ready to close: Yes", run `reSort`, assert the audit is still fresh (`auditedAt >= updatedAt` holds / freshness check passes) and `updatedAt` is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression test: a genuine semantic edit after audit still invalidates freshness (existing WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 behavior preserved).
- [ ] Existing re-sort / sync / audit tests pass; full suite green.

## Constraints

- Surgical change in `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` + `packages/shared/src/database.ts` only. No schema migration.
- Check sibling: WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt) — fix here must not conflict; note interaction in a comment.

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769` — `batchUpdateSortIndices`
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts:755-793` — re-sort paths; `:644` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh`; `:2215` — recency scoring
- `src/commands/re-sort.ts`

## Related work

- WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 (freshness rule — preserve for semantic edits)
- WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (sibling timestamp symptom)
- WL-0MM4OA55D1741ETF, WL-0MOYD0UAC003YJA3, WL-0MNX9XIQD005PUVW (auto re-sort features)
- Victim example: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V

Discovered-from: WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH.

When the audit runner runs child audits in separate-process mode (`--no-child-in-main-slot`), each child Phase-1 AC screen spawned a pi subprocess whose output could not be parsed: 'Warning: Unparseable Pi output for AC evaluation — falling back to partial verdict'. All child ACs were persisted as partial ('Ready to close: No'), which then reverted the in_review children to open/plan_complete and (via dependency reconciliation) to blocked — cascading a parent audit to 'Ready to close: No' even though the parent's own ACs were all met.

The default in-main-slot mode avoids this (child screens are performed by the invoking session), which is how the parent was ultimately verified green. Suggest: make separate-process child screening resilient to the local-proxy output format (or detect the unparseable case and retry/escalate instead of persisting partial), so the mode is usable in this environment.

# Intake Brief — Smart Audit Re-instatement

**Headline:** When the audit freshness check (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) flags an audit as stale, the system should automatically review the changes made since the audit and decide whether to re-instate the original audit or flag the item for re-audit — rather than treating all post-audit changes as requiring a full re-run.

## Problem statement

Audits are invalidated whenever a work item's `updatedAt` changes after the audit time (`isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`). However, many changes do not affect the code or implementation that was audited (e.g., changing a comment, updating assignee). The audit skill should automatically inspect the changes since the audit and decide whether to re-instate the original audit or require a new one.

**Producer clarification:** The system should inspect anything that changes the intent of the work item or actions taken against it — description, comments, audit text, dependencies, commit messages.

## Users

- **Developers using `wl next` / Pi TUI:** Audited items should not be unnecessarily re-audited when changes are irrelevant to the implementation.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher:** Should not re-dispatch items that were recently audited and whose changes are non-semantic.
- **Producers:** A "Ready to close: Yes" item should stay ready unless changes actually affect the audit outcome.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Automatic re-instatement detection:** When `isAuditNotReadyFresh` returns `false` (audit flagged as stale), the system automatically inspects the changes made since `auditedAt` and decides whether to re-instate the audit or flag for re-audit.
2. **Change inspection covers key fields:** The inspection examines description, comments, audit text, dependencies, and commit messages for changes that could affect the audit outcome. Non-semantic changes (e.g., metadata-only updates) do not trigger re-audit.
3. **Re-instatement logic:** If changes are deemed non-semantic (no impact on audit outcome), the original audit is re-instated by resetting `updatedAt` to `auditedAt` (same pattern as `saveAuditResult`). If changes are semantic, the audit is flagged as needing re-run.
4. **Full project test suite passes** with new regression tests covering re-instatement of non-semantic changes and re-audit flag for semantic changes.

## Constraints

- Change confined to audit freshness logic in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and the audit result management in the persistent store.
- No schema changes required.
- Must preserve existing audit behavior for items with no previous audit.
- Must be fully automatic — no operator intervention required.

## Existing state

- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:644`** — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`. If false, the audit is treated as stale.
- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:1038`** — `saveAuditResult` resets `updatedAt = auditedAt` to keep audits fresh after audit writes.
- **`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`** — Audit results stored in SQLite; `getAllAuditResults` / `saveAuditResult` methods.

## Desired change

1. Create a new function `assessAuditInvalidate(changesSinceAudited, auditResult)` that inspects the delta between the audit time and current state.
2. The function should classify changes as semantic (affect audit outcome) or non-semantic (no impact).
3. For non-semantic changes, re-instate the audit (reset `updatedAt = auditedAt`).
4. For semantic changes, mark the audit as needing re-run.
5. Integrate into the `wl next` / TUI flow where audit freshness is checked.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` (line 644), audit map builder, sorting logic
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — Audit storage methods, `batchUpdateSortIndices` (line 747-769)
- `packages/shared/src/sync.ts` — Sync merge logic
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — Audit command integration point
- `src/pi-audit.ts` — Pi audit module

## Related work

- **WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO** — Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations (complementary; prevents timestamp churn, this handles post-invalidation review)
- **WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA** — Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn (child of WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO)
- **WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5** — Established the audit freshness rule (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Semantic boundary ambiguity:** What counts as a semantic change is subjective. **Assumption:** Changes to description, comments, dependencies, and commit messages are semantic; changes to assignee, tags, priority, and sortIndex are non-semantic. Document the rule in code comments.
- **Scope creep:** Requests for configurable invalidation policies. **Mitigation:** Keep this to the concrete scenarios identified; file separate items for broader policy changes.
- **Performance risk:** Inspecting changes since audit could add overhead. **Mitigation:** Only run when freshness check fails; use efficient diff comparison.
- **Backward compatibility:** Existing audit behavior must be preserved for items with no previous audit result.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What specific change types should the audit skill inspect when deciding whether to re-instate an audit? — A: Anything that changes the intent of the work item or actions taken against it. So description, comments, audit text, dependencies, commit messages etc. Source: interactive reply (producer).
- Q: Should this be automatic (triggered when an invalidated audit is discovered) or manual (operator/producer-initiated)? — A: Automatic. Source: interactive reply (producer).
- Q: How does this relate to WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO (Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations)? — A: Complementary — WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO prevents timestamp churn from invalidating audits, this item handles post-invalidation review to determine whether to re-instate or re-run. Source: interactive reply (producer).

Currently non-blocking: the full suite is green (the affected assertions do not depend on the missed branch), so this is hardening, not a live failure. Discovered from: WL-0MU2FM1L60002URI.

# Log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch panes, except implement

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher creates panes for each work item it dispatches (intake, plan, audit, risk-effort), but panes stay open indefinitely until an operator closes them manually. There is no automatic pane lifecycle management — completed panes clutter the Dispatcher workspace and the dispatch log lacks pane-close status updates (intake complete, plan complete, audit passed/failed, or stuck). This work item adds automatic pane closing and enhanced logging for pane lifecycle events.

## Users

- **Operator** — wants the Dispatcher workspace to stay tidy; auto-closed panes reduce manual cleanup.
- **Producer** — wants a clear audit trail of pane outcomes in the dispatch log: which panes completed successfully, which are stuck, and which failed their audit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** The downtime worker logs every pane-close event to `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` with: ISO timestamp, work item ID, work item title, pane ID, dispatch kind (`plan`/`intake`/`audit`/`risk-effort`), and outcome (`closed-as-intake-complete`, `closed-as-plan-complete`, `audit-passed`, `audit-failed`, `requires-attention`).
- **AC2:** When a dispatched item's stage advances to `intake_complete` or `plan_complete`, the worker records the appropriate log entry and closes the associated pane (except for `kind === 'implement'` items).
- **AC3:** When a dispatched item is left in any other state (e.g. `in_review` without reaching a terminal state, or blocked by producer questions where `needsProducerReview === true`), the worker records a `requires-attention` log entry with a summary reason.
- **AC4:** When a dispatched item reaches `in_review` status (implementation completed), the worker records the event in the log.
- **AC5:** When an audit pane completes and the item's audit status is recorded (`auditedAt` set, audit passed or failed), the worker records the audit outcome in the log and closes the pane (audit panes are always auto-closed regardless of the `implement` exception).
- **AC6:** The `implement` kind is EXCLUDED from all auto-close logic — implement panes remain open until manually closed by the operator.
- **AC7:** All logging and pane-closing operations are fail-closed: a failed log write or pane-close attempt must never crash the worker or block subsequent dispatches.
- **AC8:** Full herdr + repo test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The existing `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` rolling JSONL format must be extended (not replaced); legacy entries remain valid.
- Pane closing must be safe — only panes that were spawned by the downtime worker for this specific work item should be closed.
- The worker must detect state changes without polling the worklog excessively; consider event-driven or reasonable polling cadence.
- The `implements` exception (AC6) is mandatory — no implement pane is ever auto-closed.

## Existing state

- Dispatch logging already exists via `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8): a bounded JSONL log recording dispatched items.
- The `AgentTracker` (`agent-tracker.ts`) already records work-item → pane-ID associations in `.worklog/agent-panes.json`.
- Panes are spawned via `send-to-pi.sh` with pane IDs that are captured and tracked.
- Panes currently stay open indefinitely — no auto-close mechanism exists.
- The worker polls `wl` commands periodically but does not track work-item state changes post-dispatch.

## Desired change

1. **Extend the dispatch log schema** to support pane-close and state-change entries with outcome reasons.
2. **Add a pane-lifecycle monitor** that tracks dispatched items after they are spawned, detecting when they reach terminal stages (`intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_review`) or when audits complete.
3. **Implement auto-close logic** that closes panes based on the detected outcome, with the `implement` exception.
4. **Log all lifecycle events** to the dispatch log with structured entries.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Core dispatch worker; add pane-lifecycle tracking and auto-close logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Extend log entry schema for pane-close outcomes.
- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` — Already tracks pane IDs; may need extension for lifecycle callbacks.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — New tests for pane-close logic.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8** — *Log herdr downtime dispatches (item comment + rolling .worklog log)* — existing dispatch logging infrastructure.
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** — *Work-item ↔ agent-pane association tracker* — `AgentTracker` that maps work items to pane IDs.
- **WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3** — *Remove client-side pane count cap* — panes now deliberately stay open until manually closed (context for why auto-close is new).
- **WL-0MTJQOZ0K007KD40** — *Dispatch-logs skill: generates 24h global dispatch report* — related observability.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should happen to panes for items that reach `in_review` but then revert to a different stage?" — Answer: Log the initial `in_review` arrival; if the pane is still open and the item changes again, log the new state. Only close panes at the specific terminal points defined in AC2–AC5. Source: intake draft.
- Q: "Does 'requires attention' apply to panes that are still actively running (agent in `working` state)?" — Answer: No — "requires attention" applies to panes where the agent session has ended (`done` state) but the work item has not reached a terminal stage (`intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_review`). Source: intake draft.
- Q: "Should the worker proactively close panes, or just log and signal?" — Answer: The worker should both log AND close the pane (except for implement). The pane close is an active action. Source: intake draft.

## Goal

As a herdr operator, I want the downtime dispatcher to open at most one pane per work item per skill while a prior dispatch is still in-flight, so concurrent agents never share a worktree/branch or fight over the same files.

## Problem Statement

On 2026-09-21 the downtime dispatcher spawned `/skill:implement` twice for two different critical items (LP-0MUAY98ZR002JBAA, LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO) within minutes-to-hours of each other. Both dispatched agents operated on the same worktree and branch concurrently, causing file conflicts, thrashed edits, discarded work, and wasted compute (~2h20m45s on LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO). This is a recurrence of WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT (prior RCA covering audit/plan tiers) in the implement tier, affecting critical-priority items.

## Users

- **Herdr operator:** Runs the herdr downtime dispatcher and expects it to correctly serialize dispatches.
- **Pi agent (AI):** Receives auto-dispatches from herdr and works on assigned items.
- **System administrator:** Monitors herdr performance and resource usage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Root cause confirmed:** The selection path and mechanism that produced the 13:54:33Z re-dispatch of LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO are confirmed (H1: critical-first scan bypasses marker exclusion / H2: stale item status in dispatcher snapshot / H3: non-atomic rolling-log rewrite / H4: multiple leaders) via targeted instrumentation or reproduction.

- **AC2 — Duplicate-dispatch prevention:** A critical-priority item is never dispatched twice for the same skill while a prior dispatch is in-flight (live pane and/or unexpired claim), regardless of marker freshness or stage advancement.

- **AC3 — Escalation preserved:** The critical-first escalation path retains its ability to progress items blocked by a stale marker, without re-dispatching in-flight items. Escalation is bounded (e.g., once per claim TTL, or gated on a live-pane / in-flight check).

- **AC4 — Atomic rolling log:** The dispatch and coordination rolling logs use atomic write (write temp file + `rename`) so a concurrent marker read can never observe an empty or partial log.

- **AC5 — Regression test:** An integration test covering both the Herdr-head and coordination dispatch paths verifies that two idle cycles with a critical implement item already claimed/in-flight at the same stage produce exactly one dispatch.

- **AC6 — Dispatcher log enriched:** Each dispatcher log entry records the session/pane id and the selection path/reason, extending the current schema (`itemId/kind/dispatchedAt/cwd/title/stage`) to support automated RCA.

## Constraints

- Changes must be in TypeScript (`packages/herdr/src/`) and use the existing dispatch marker lifecycle.
- The rolling log must remain human-readable JSONL.
- Escalation for stuck critical items must not be eliminated — only the duplicate-dispatch bug must be fixed.
- The fix should work within the existing single-leader model; multi-leader support is out of scope.

## Existing State

- Dispatcher selection uses two paths: (1) normal Herdr-head scan via `classifyItemForDispatch` (filters `status === 'open'`, consults dispatched-marker exclusion), and (2) critical-first scan via `dispatchClaimedTier` (CAS claim only, bypasses marker exclusion).
- Dispatched markers (`downtime-log.ts:273,310`) exclude items only while `marker.stage === itemStage` AND age ≤ staleness window (default 24h, hard floor 1h, ceiling 7d).
- The critical-first scan intentionally bypasses marker exclusion at `downtime-worker.ts:1935-1966`.
- Rolling logs are rewritten non-atomically (read-all → append → trim → write), creating a TOCTOU window.
- The first dispatch of each duplicate pair claimed the item (`status: in_progress`) but the stage stayed `plan_complete` (a prior `WARNING: Failed to update stage`).
- WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN added conditional claim + plan/intake marker exclusion (completed). This is the implement-tier recurrence.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Dispatcher selection and dispatch logic (critical-first scan at ~line 1895, normal scan at ~line 2455, dispatch site at ~line 2710-2745)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Dispatched markers and rolling log management (markers at ~line 273, 310; appendRollingJsonl at ~line 411-431)
- `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py` — Canonical tool for scanning duplicate dispatches

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT** — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (completed) — prior audit/plan-tier RCA.
- **WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN** — Downtime dispatcher: conditional claim + plan/intake marker exclusion (completed) — implement-tier fix for a different path.
- **WL-0MT32F908002YFFA** — Downtime dispatch: recover items stranded by marker-write-failed or spawn failure (open) — interacts with marker lifecycle.
- **WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY** — Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions (completed).
- Code-referenced: WL-0MU6UL0RJ008IHGT (marker staleness), WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT (critical-first scan), WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 (Herdr-list-head dispatch).

## Out of Scope

- Other pre-existing duplicate pairs from before 2026-09-21.
- The correctness of code delivered by LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO (already merged to `dev`).
- Multi-leader/leader-failover support for the dispatcher.

## Risks & Assumptions

**Risks:**
- Changing the critical-first scan to consult markers may slow escalation of genuinely blocked critical items. *Mitigation:* bound escalation with a TTL or in-flight check (AC3).
- Atomic log rewrite changes file semantics; existing consumers must handle it. *Mitigation:* JSONL format preserved, `rename` is transparent.
- Regression test requires simulating dispatch cycles; test complexity may be high. *Mitigation:* leverage existing Herdr test infrastructure.

**Assumptions:**
- `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` is the authoritative dispatch record.
- The 13:54:33Z dispatch was not a legitimate operator-initiated retry.
- Single-leader model holds; no concurrent workers on this instance.
- The `status: in_progress` claim by the first agent was the only serialisation mechanism — the stage never advanced, so marker exclusion never released the item.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

1. **Q:** Is this item scoped to both root-cause analysis AND implementation, or should it be split into an investigation item + a fix item?
   - **A (agent):** Single item is appropriate. The description already contains sufficient investigation to proceed to fix; the investigation is tightly coupled to the fix (AC1 confirms the mechanism before AC2-AC5 implement it). Splitting adds overhead without benefit.
   - **Source:** Agent assessment during intake review.

2. **Q:** For AC3, should escalation of items blocked by stale markers be bound to a fixed interval (e.g., once per 24h) or to a more dynamic mechanism (e.g., check for live pane before re-dispatching)?
   - **A (agent):** Dynamic mechanism is preferred — checking for a live pane / in-flight claim is more robust than a fixed interval. A fixed interval risks either too-frequent checks (wasted cycles) or too-rare checks (stalled items).
   - **Source:** Agent recommendation based on code analysis of the marker lifecycle.

3. **Q:** Should the regression test be a unit test or an integration test?
   - **A (agent):** Integration test — the bug involves the interaction between the dispatcher loop, marker management, and claim lifecycle, which spans multiple functions in the runtime loop.
   - **Source:** Agent assessment of the failure mode.

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I need the 13:54:33Z re-dispatch of LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO traced to a specific
selection path and mechanism, so the fix targets the real code path instead of a hypothesis.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4** (RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches CRITICAL implement
items). Covers parent **AC1**.

# Context

Planning established that the hypothesis set in the parent description is not sufficient on its own:
the Herdr-head critical-first scan (`selectCriticalFirstCandidates`) only accepts
`status === 'open' || 'blocked'` items, and `dispatchClaimedTier` performs a CAS claim on the
expected `status`+`stage`. A duplicate therefore requires the item to be **genuinely `open` at the
expected stage** at re-dispatch time — i.e. H1 (marker bypass) alone cannot duplicate; H2/H5 (the
item's `status` reverts to `open` while a dispatch pane is still live) is the necessary partner. That
is exactly the scenario the escalation path was built for, and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
already documents it ("a previous dispatch was rolled back / the implementing agent aborted and reset
the item to `open` while the standing marker remained").

The incident root log is **not present on this host**: `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py`
over the five default roots finds no `LP-*` entries at all. AC1 must therefore be satisfied by
targeted instrumentation and reproduction, which AC1 explicitly sanctions.

Also note the second dispatch vector: the coordination leader "validates offers at dispatch-time
without a marker check" (same doc), so the coordination path must be traced too.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC1.1 — RED witness.** A characterisation test drives **two idle cycles** in one process against a
critical `plan_complete` (implement-kind) item that is observed `open` at its marker's stage while its
dispatch pane is live, and asserts exactly `1` dispatch. The test **fails** against the pre-fix code
and records the observed dispatch count.

**AC1.2 — Confirmed selection path.** The RCA verdict names the confirmed selection path (Herdr-head
critical-first scan vs coordination offer dispatch) with a source line reference and a cycle-by-cycle
trace (cycle 1: selected/accepted, cycle 2: selected/accepted + claim outcome + marker state).

**AC1.3 — Hypothesis decision table.** Each of H1 (critical-first bypasses marker exclusion), H2
(stale item status in the dispatcher snapshot), H3 (non-atomic rolling-log rewrite), H4 (multiple
leaders) and H5 (item `status` reverted to `open` while a pane is live) is marked **confirmed** /
**refuted** / **not reproducible**, each with the discriminating evidence. H2/H5 is explicitly
confirmed or refuted.

**AC1.4 — Residual uncertainty.** Any hypothesis left open is recorded with the workaround F3/F4
apply for it, and the residual risk is stated.

**AC1.5 — CAS/bypass analysis recorded.** The verdict states whether the duplicate required a real
DB `status: open` (CAS succeeds) or a CAS gap, so F3's guard is justified rather than assumed.

# Minimal implementation

- Add a deterministic two-cycle harness around `dispatchDowntimeWork` using the existing injectable
  seams: `getHerdrListHead`, `getNextItem`, `claimItem`, `spawnAgentPane`, `recordDispatch`,
  `getRunningDowntimePanes`.
- Simulate the live pane via the `herdr pane list` fixture path (`parseHerdrPaneListOutput` /
  `countRunningDowntimePanes`) so the same data shape the dispatcher sees in production is used.
- Simulate the status revert by returning the item as `open` in cycle 2's Herdr head while the marker
  written in cycle 1 stands.
- Capture the per-cycle selection reason (a precursor to the AC6 schema) so the verdict is auditable.
- **Parent AC1 (restated):** The selection path and mechanism that produced the 13:54:33Z re-dispatch of LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO are confirmed (H1: critical-first scan bypasses marker exclusion / H2: stale item status in dispatcher snapshot / H3: non-atomic rolling-log rewrite / H4: multiple leaders) via targeted instrumentation or reproduction.

# Dependencies

None. This is the first item in the sequence.

# Deliverables

- RCA verdict comment on parent WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4 (decision table + trace + line references).
- New test block in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (the RED witness; promoted to the
  permanent suite by WL-WL-0MUBVKS5I007LSWB).

# Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`
- `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

- Implementing the fix (WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO/WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI).

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I need a permanent regression suite proving that two idle cycles over a critical

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want the critical-first escalation to skip an item that already has a live
dispatch pane, so a critical item whose `status` reverted to `open` is never dispatched twice, while
escalation of genuinely stuck critical items is preserved.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Covers parent **AC2** and **AC3**.

# Design (approved at the plan approval gate)

The critical-first scan currently bypasses the dispatched-marker exclusion **unconditionally**
(WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT). This replaces the unconditional bypass with a **stale-only bypass gated on an
item-scoped live-pane check**, with a marker-TTL fallback when the pane query is unavailable:

```
for a critical-first candidate:
  1. resolve the item-scoped in-flight signal (live dispatch pane whose label suffix is the item id
     and whose agent status is non-terminal)
  2. if a live WORKING pane exists                 -> SKIP  (reason: in-flight-pane)
  3. else if the pane query SUCCEEDED and found none -> ESCALATE (reason: no-live-pane)
  4. else (pane query FAILED/unparseable)          -> fall back to the marker TTL:
       fresh marker (age <= markerStaleWindowMs)   -> SKIP  (reason: in-flight-unverified)
       stale/absent marker                         -> ESCALATE (reason: marker-stale-escalation)
```

This deliberate **neither-blind-fail-closed-nor-blind-fail-open** choice was confirmed at the approval
gate: escalation is never starved permanently (the TTL fallback keeps progressing), and a duplicate is
never permitted while a pane is live. Note the fallback is benign in practice — pane spawn itself needs
herdr, so a persistent pane-query failure also prevents dispatch.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC2.1 — Live pane blocks.** With a live `working` downtime pane whose label suffix is the item id,
**no** dispatch is attempted for that item — regardless of marker freshness, stage advancement, or
`status` being `open`.

**AC2.2 — Fail-closed on unknown in-flight state.** A failed or unparseable pane query never results in
a dispatch that could duplicate in-flight work; it resolves via the marker-TTL fallback (AC3.3) and
records the `in-flight-unverified` reason.

**AC2.3 — Terminal panes do not block.** Panes whose agent is absent, `done`, or `exited` do not block
dispatch (no idle-pane deadlock).

**AC2.4 — Item-scoped only.** The guard never uses a global running-pane count as a dispatch limit —
the WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3 invariant is preserved (that count stays a liveness/owner-lease signal only).

**AC2.5 — Normal loop covered.** The guard also applies to critical candidates reaching dispatch
through the normal (non-critical-first) loop, so AC2 holds "regardless of selection path".

**AC3.1 — Escalation preserved.** A critical item with a fresh **or** stale marker and **no** live pane
is still escalated within one idle cycle; all existing critical-first tests stay green.

**AC3.2 — Escalation is bounded.** Deferral happens only while a live working pane exists or while the
marker is fresh during a pane-query outage — never by an unbounded fixed TTL alone.

**AC3.3 — TTL fallback documented.** The fallback bound (`markerStaleWindowMs`, default 24h, floor 1h)
and its rationale are documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

# Minimal implementation

- Add an item-scoped in-flight resolver, resolved **once per idle cycle** and threaded into
  `dispatchFromHerdrList`: extend `RunningPanesResult` to expose pane records (or add a sibling dep
  returning `{paneId, itemId, kind, agentStatus}[]`), reusing `parseHerdrPaneListOutput`.
- Derive the item id from the pane label suffix (`buildDowntimePaneTitle` preserves `- <itemId>` as a
  suffix via `truncatePaneTitlePreservingSuffix`).
- Replace the critical-first loop's unconditional marker bypass with the decision table above.
- Factor the resolver so WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI can reuse it unchanged (no logic duplication across paths).
- Fail-open on resolver errors in the sense that the resolver returns "unavailable" (never throws into
  the dispatch loop); fail-closed semantics are the decision table's step 4.
- **Parent AC2 (restated):** A critical-priority item is never dispatched twice for the same skill while a prior dispatch is in-flight (live pane and/or unexpired claim), regardless of marker freshness or stage advancement.
- **Parent AC3 (restated):** The critical-first escalation path retains its ability to progress items blocked by a stale marker, without re-dispatching in-flight items. Escalation is bounded (e.g., once per claim TTL, or gated on a live-pane / in-flight check).

# Dependencies

- WL-WL-0MUBVKS5I007LSWB (regression suite — must exist to prove AC5.5's RED→GREEN transition).

# Deliverables

- Code + unit tests + `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` update (§"Critical-first tier & freeze
  split-by-skill").
- RED→GREEN evidence comment referencing the WL-WL-0MUBVKS5I007LSWB suite.

- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts`

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want the dispatch and coordination rolling logs written atomically, so a
concurrent marker read can never observe an empty or partial log and momentarily lose a
duplicate-dispatch marker.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Covers parent **AC4**.

# Context

`appendRollingJsonl` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`) rewrites the log non-atomically: read all
lines → push → trim → `writeFile` directly to the target path. A reader arriving during the
`writeFile` can see a truncated or empty file, which makes `dispatchedItemMarkers` /
`dispatchedItemStages` momentarily lose the marker. This is a contributing factor (H3 in the parent
RCA), not the sole cause — it cannot by itself duplicate a critical-tier item, because the
critical-first scan bypasses markers entirely (that is WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO's fix). It is fixed independently
because it is a genuine TOCTOU defect and because it silently weakens every marker-guarded tier.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC4.1 — Atomic replacement.** `appendRollingJsonl` writes to a temporary sibling file and `rename`s it
over the target. A test asserts the target path is never opened for direct writing.

**AC4.2 — No leaked temp files.** No temporary file remains after a successful append, and none remains
after an I/O failure (cleanup happens before the error is rethrown).

**AC4.3 — Concurrent reader never sees a partial log.** A test that hammers append + read in parallel
observes **only** complete, parseable JSONL lines — never an empty file, never a partial line. The test
fails against the pre-fix writer.

**AC4.4 — Contract unchanged.** Trimming to `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES` (100) and the throw-on-I/O-failure
(fail-closed) contract are unchanged; the file stays human-readable JSONL.

**AC4.5 — Both logs.** Both `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` and the coordination log use the atomic
writer.

**AC4.6 — Same-filesystem rename.** The temp file is created in the same directory as the target so
`rename` is atomic (a cross-device rename would fall back to copy + unlink and lose atomicity).

# Minimal implementation

- Temp file name including pid + random suffix, in the same directory as the target.
- `mkdir(dir, {recursive:true})` unchanged; `readFile`/trim/append logic unchanged; `writeFile` to the
  temp path, then `rename` over the target.
- `try`/`finally`-style cleanup: on any error, best-effort unlink the temp file, then rethrow so the
  caller's fail-closed behaviour (abort the dispatch) is preserved.
- Keep the existing exported signatures so no caller changes are needed.
- **Parent AC4 (restated):** The dispatch and coordination rolling logs use atomic write (write temp file + `rename`) so a concurrent marker read can never observe an empty or partial log.

# Dependencies

None — independently shippable and may land in parallel with WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO/WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI.

# Deliverables

- Code + tests + `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §"Rolling log trimming" update.

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts`

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want every dispatcher log entry to record the session/pane id and the selection
path/reason, so the next duplicate-dispatch RCA is answerable from the log alone instead of by
inference.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Covers parent **AC6**.

# Context

The current schema is `itemId/kind/dispatchedAt/cwd/title/stage`. Two constraints shape the design:

1. `recordDispatch` runs **before** `spawnAgentPane` (fail-closed ordering: a marker write failure
   aborts the dispatch), and `DowntimeSpawnResult` is `{ok: true}` with no pane id — `send-to-pi.sh` is
   fire-and-forget. The pane/session id is therefore **not** known at marker-write time.
2. `dispatchedItemMarkers` takes the **last** entry per `itemId`, and `markerStillExcludes` is
   fail-closed on a missing/unparseable `dispatchedAt`. Any post-spawn entry must therefore **preserve**
   `dispatchedAt` + `stage` or it would corrupt marker semantics.

Decision at the plan approval gate (Q5): use a **best-effort post-spawn enrichment entry** rather than
extending the spawn contract / `send-to-pi.sh`.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC6.1 — Selection path and reason recorded.** Every successful dispatch entry records
`selectionPath` (e.g. `critical-first` | `normal-scan` | `coordination-offer` | `scheduled-prompt`) and
a machine-readable `selectionReason` (e.g. `marker-stale`, `in-flight-pane`, `no-live-pane`,
`in-flight-unverified`, `non-critical`).

**AC6.2 — Pane/session id recorded without breaking markers.** Successful dispatches record the
resolved pane id via a post-spawn enrichment entry that **preserves** `itemId`, `kind`, `stage` and
`dispatchedAt`; a test round-trips the enriched log through `dispatchedItemMarkers` and
`markerStillExcludes` and proves identical exclusion/release behaviour with and without enrichment.

**AC6.3 — Enrichment is fail-open.** If the pane id cannot be resolved, the dispatch still succeeds and
the log records an explicit absence (no guessed value).

**AC6.4 — Backward compatible.** Legacy entries without the new fields parse and behave exactly as
before; the existing `downtime-log.test.ts` compatibility tests stay green.

**AC6.5 — Tooling reports the new fields.** `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py` surfaces
`selectionPath`/`selectionReason`/`paneId` for post-fix evidence (and tolerates their absence).

**AC6.6 — Spawn-failed entries unchanged.** `outcome: 'spawn-failed'` entries stay non-excluding
(WL-0MT32F908002YFFA AC2 invariant) with or without the new fields.

# Minimal implementation

- Add `selectionPath`, `selectionReason` and an optional `paneId` to `DowntimeDispatchEvent`.
- Thread the selection path/reason from the selection loops (WL-WL-0MUBVKPLP006RRDJ's per-cycle trace provides the
  vocabulary; WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO/WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI provide the in-flight reasons).
- After a successful spawn, resolve the pane id (label-suffix lookup against `herdr pane list`) and
  append the enrichment entry, swallowing errors exactly like the existing spawn-failed trace.
- Extend the scan script's output fields and the documented log schema.
- **Parent AC6 (restated):** Each dispatcher log entry records the session/pane id and the selection path/reason, extending the current schema (`itemId/kind/dispatchedAt/cwd/title/stage`) to support automated RCA.

# Dependencies

- WL-WL-0MUBVKPLP006RRDJ (defines the selection-path/reason vocabulary from the confirmed mechanism).

# Deliverables

- Code + tests + `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` log-schema update + scan-script field support.

# Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts`

# Ship-mode guard: block entry while project work is in progress, freeze on confirm

**Headline:** The herdr worklist gains a pre-dialog guard that refuses to open the Ship It confirmation dialog while any live agent pane (any workspace) is working on a work item belonging to the project, listing the blocking panes/work items; on `ship` confirmation it writes the Code Freeze marker immediately and clears it if the release command fails to dispatch.

## Problem statement

The herdr worklist lets an operator enter Ship It (dev→main release) mode even while other agent panes are actively working on the same project, risking a release of half-finished work. The worklist must refuse to open the Ship It confirmation dialog while any live agent pane in any workspace is working on a work item belonging to the project being shipped, tell the operator which panes/work items are blocking, and — once the operator confirms with `ship` — place the project into Code Freeze immediately (before the release command is dispatched).

## Users

- **Producers / release managers** using the herdr worklist who trigger dev→main releases.
- **Other agents** working on the project, who rely on the Code Freeze marker to refuse new implementation while a release is running.
- **User story:** "As a producer, when I press `S` to ship, I want the worklist to refuse and tell me which panes are still working so I do not ship over in-flight work. Once I have closed them and type `ship`, I want the freeze to apply at once so no agent starts new work mid-release."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Pressing the Ship It shortcut (`S`) when one or more **live** agent panes (machine-wide, across all herdr workspaces) carry a work-item ID belonging to the current project's worklog does **not** open the Ship It confirmation dialog. A notice is shown instead listing the offending work-item IDs (and pane labels where available) and stating that ship mode cannot be entered until the work is completed and those panes are closed.
- [ ] The blocking check runs **before** the confirmation dialog is rendered; the dialog is never shown while blocking panes exist.
- [ ] A pane only blocks when it hosts a **live** agent: a pane whose agent is absent, `done`, or `exited` does not block, even when its label carries a project work-item ID.
- [ ] When no blocking pane exists, pressing `S` opens the Ship It confirmation dialog exactly as today (no regression), and typing `ship` + Enter dispatches `/skill:ship release` as before.
- [ ] On typing `ship` + Enter (the confirm action), the worklist writes the Code Freeze marker at `<worklog-dir>/code-freeze.json` with `{ "active": true, "reason": "...", "startedAt": "<ISO>", "pid": <pid> }` **before** dispatching `/skill:ship release`.
- [ ] If dispatching `/skill:ship release` fails (no agent pane available, `onCommand` throws, or the dispatch is a no-op), the worklist **best-effort removes the Code Freeze marker it just wrote** and surfaces the error, so no stale freeze blocks the project once the release never started.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: the guard with blocking and non-blocking pane sets (live vs `done`/`exited` agents), multiple blocking panes, work-item IDs from a different project not blocking, the blocked-notice content, the pre-dialog gating (dialog not opened when blocked), the marker write on confirm, and the marker cleanup on dispatch failure.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and the Code Freeze marker contract docs.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Fail-open for browsing, fail-safe for the guard.** The existing Code Freeze reads are deliberately fail-open (a broken marker never blocks browsing). The new guard must fail *closed* only in the sense of not shipping on ambiguous pane data: an unreadable `herdr pane list` or `wl list` must not silently allow the ship dialog — surface the uncertainty rather than pretending the project is clear. (Decide and document the exact behaviour in implementation; recommendation: treat an unavailable pane/item query as "cannot verify — do not ship" and show the notice.)
- **No new dependency.** Reuse the existing primitives: `parseHerdrPaneListOutput` / `HerdrPaneRecord` (`downtime-worker.ts`), `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` (`hydrator.ts`), and the `code-freeze.ts` marker contract.
- **Project membership by work-item ID, not prefix.** Match pane-label IDs against the actual set of work-item IDs in the current project's worklog. A shared ID prefix across projects must not cause a false block.
- **Code Freeze marker ownership changes.** The marker is currently written/cleared by the ship skill and only read by the herdr plugin. This work extends the contract so the plugin writes the marker on Ship It confirmation; the ship skill remains the authority that clears it on release exit. Update the contract documentation accordingly.
- **No regression to the Ship It dialog.** The typed-confirmation behaviour (case-insensitive `ship`, Enter to confirm, Esc to cancel, bottom-anchored overlay) is unchanged.
- **ANSI rendering.** Any notice reuses the existing in-pane notice/dialog rendering helpers (`formatCodeFreezeDialog` pattern); no new dependencies.
- Follow build → test → commit discipline (vitest suite in `packages/herdr`).

## Existing state

- **Ship It shortcut / dialog** — `packages/herdr/src/ship-it-dialog.ts` (`ShipItDialogState`, `formatShipItDialog`, `overlayShipItDialog`) and `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (`SHIP_IT_COMMAND = '/skill:ship release'`, `openShipItDialog()`, dialog key handling in `onData`). The dialog is opened from the chord-resolution branch when the resolved command equals `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`.
- **Code Freeze marker** — `packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.ts` provides read-only helpers (`readCodeFreezeState`, `isCodeFreezeActive`, `readCodeFreezeStatus`, `readCodeFreezeStatusForRoot`) for `.worklog/code-freeze.json`; there is currently **no writer** in the plugin. The ship skill writes/clears the marker around the release.
- **Project ↔ pane matching** — `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` already lists in-progress items (`wl list --status in-progress`) and active panes (`herdr pane list`, machine-wide) and matches work-item IDs embedded in pane labels via `extractWorkItemIdsFromText`. `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` guarantees spawned pane titles preserve the work-item ID suffix, so labels reliably carry the ID.
- **Blocked-work UI precedent** — the Code Freeze notice (`code-freezeNotice` flag, `formatCodeFreezeDialog`, dismissal key handling in `worklist.ts`) is a full-pane modal used when an implement action is blocked.
- **Toast feedback** — `packages/herdr/src/notify.ts` (`showToast`) is fire-and-forget and may not be reliably seen; a blocking guard should use the in-pane modal notice pattern instead.

## Desired change

1. **New guard module** (e.g. `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts`): pure, injectable helpers to
   - collect the current project's work-item IDs from `wl list --json`;
   - list machine-wide panes from `herdr pane list` (reusing `parseHerdrPaneListOutput`);
   - return the **blocking** panes: panes whose label carries a project work-item ID and whose agent is live (agent present, status not `done`/`exited`);
   - format the blocked-notice text listing the offending work-item IDs / pane labels.
   Unit-test the pure logic with fixture panes (no real `wl`/`herdr`).
2. **Pre-dialog gate in `worklist.ts`**: when the resolved command is `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, run the guard *before* `openShipItDialog()`. If blocking panes exist, set a modal notice (listing the panes) and return without opening the dialog. The notice dismisses like the Code Freeze notice (Esc/Enter/q) and never dispatches.
